The hardness over tensile strength ratio is /C243.13 ± 0.39 in the current alloys, similar to that in conventional steels [22], and obeys well the Tabor relationship [23].

In the (AlCoCrFeNi)100-xNix HEA system, the volume fraction and fracture strain increased with increasing Ni content. The lattice constants increased up to 4 at.% of Ni but decreased beyond that due to excessive addition causing large lattice distortion energy, resulting in crystal transformation.

The increase in ductility of HEAs V0, V0.5, and V1.0 is attributed to grain refinement and uniformity of alloy element distribution. However, the V content reaching V1.5 significantly deteriorates tensile strength and ductility.

Most of the equiatomic alloys described in the literature do not consist of a single solid solution phase; instead, they contain multiple phases, including secondary solid solution phases and/or intermetallic compounds. Measured mechanical properties represent composite responses of the multiphase microstructures.
